publication_and_access: Greenberg and Keinan 2009, West Bank Archaeological Database (XLSX; hash in kohlit/README.md) and its sourcebook (open PDF)
periods_sought: As each source survey reports them; terms are collated, e.g. Hasmonean to Hel and Herodian to Early Roman (p. 17)
feature_classes_sought: Sites. Site_Components 'briefly notes the principal discoveries at the site' (p. 17). Isolated structures, caves and installations are handled inconsistently, and some separate lists were left out (p. 14).
field_method: None of its own: it compiles published surveys and excavation reports (pp. 11-15). Most source surveys follow the ASI method: teams of 2-7 walkers 50-200 m apart; wadi beds and rocky or overgrown ground often get only cursory study (p. 12). Published full-coverage surveys cover over 70% of the region (p. 11).
search_unit: The source survey's site, held as one central grid point (p. 16)
position_recording: Old Israel Grid central point, 6-12 digits (p. 16)
feature_recording: Free text in Site_Components and Comments (pp. 16-18). No count field and no absence field.
absence_statement_form: None. The format cannot state an absence.
what_absences_cover: Nothing. A missing component means only that it was not listed among the principal discoveries.
notes: In most surveys field installations are 'at best, attached to the nearest site' (p. 13).

publication_and_access: Finkelstein, Lederman and Bunimovitz 1997, Highlands of Many Cultures (TAU Monograph 14), open access PDF
periods_sought: All periods, dated by diagnostic sherds only; Roman is not subdivided (pp. 18-19)
feature_classes_sought: Settlement sites and seasonal sites (p. 12). Tombs, cisterns, quarries, presses and caves were recorded in relation to central sites; isolated ones went to unpublished lists (p. 12). The 585-site total excludes water cisterns (p. 11).
field_method: First, visits to the sites marked on maps (392 of 401). Then, 1983/4-1987, a full-coverage pedestrian survey of about 70% of the grid (p. 11). Ridges, spurs, valley margins and spring areas got special emphasis; steep rocky slopes less (p. 13). 5-7 surveyors spread over each site and collected pottery over it and its slopes; the effort went into pottery, not architecture (p. 13).
search_unit: The site, numbered by its 1 km square on the 1:20,000 map sheet; coverage is stated per map sheet (pp. 14-15)
position_recording: Israel and UTM grid to 50 m; the centre of a large site (p. 16)
feature_recording: Fixed fields (type, geographic unit, elevation, size, topography, distance to springs taken from maps, previous surveys, periods) and a free-text Description (pp. 16-22). No cistern or tomb field.
what_absences_cover: Nothing about cisterns or tombs: the entries were not designed to list them at each site.
notes: When citing Mandate-era files, the author ignored references to rock-cut tombs, because such tombs occur at almost every site (p. 22). No site plans are published (p. 22).

source_type: Zertal, Manasseh Hill Country Survey, Vols. II-IV entries
publication_and_access: Zertal 1996, Zertal and Mirkam 2000 and Zertal 2005 (Hebrew), read in Brill's English editions, Vols. II (2008), III and IV (2017); PDFs supplied by the project owner, hashes in stage2/addendum_s2/source2_zertal_access.csv
methods_pages: Vol. II pp. 2, 7-9 and Index 3, pp. 772-782; Vol. III pp. 1-2 and Index 4, pp. 565-571; Vol. IV pp. 2 and 4 (the method is 'described in detail in Volume 1', which was not supplied)
periods_sought: All periods; pottery recorded by period and percentage (Vol. II p. 8)
feature_classes_sought: Sites, 'places where people dwelt', and features (agricultural installations, cisterns, roads, terraces); each type 'was surveyed and published differently' (Vol. II p. 7).
field_method: The survey was made 'on foot with no omissions', and 'all sites and features were recorded' (Vol. II p. 7), with aerial photographs. Teams of 3-12 (Vol. II p. 2) or 10-15 (Vol. III p. 2). No walker spacing or transect is stated.
search_unit: Landscape units of 10-70 sq km (Vol. II p. 7); the published record is one entry per site
position_recording: Israel grid and UTM, four digits each (100 m)
feature_recording: A two-column data block of fixed fields, then a description of the visible surface remains (Vol. II pp. 8-9). Item 11 gives the number of cistern openings, the nearest perennial water source and the nearest road (p. 8). Features outside sites: a 'partial list' in Vol. II (pp. 772-782), a list in Vol. III (pp. 565-571), none in Vol. IV.
what_absences_cover: The site record only: no cistern openings within the site area, which is the area on which structures stood (Vol. II p. 8). The field does not name caves, silos or shafts. Features outside the site appear, if at all, in the feature lists.
notes: For Vol. IV units (47 read; 18 of the 30 C2 FAILs, 15 of the 19 in the main set) the survey publishes no feature list, so the 1 km sector has no published record beyond the entries of neighbouring sites.

publication_and_access: Conder and Kitchener, The Survey of Western Palestine, Memoirs Vols. II-III (1882-83), archive.org OCR text; Vol. I read for the method (archive.org surveyofwesternp01conduoft)
methods_pages: Mem I pp. 29-31 (method of the survey), 37-38 (how the memoirs were written), 41 (sections of each memoir)
absences_coded_A_and_B: 2 (one statement, S676, coded by A and by B)
periods_sought: No systematic period recording; the officers describe 'ancient remains' and date some by architecture or sources
feature_classes_sought: Section A: villages and topography; Section B: 'a detailed account of the ancient remains' of the sheet (Mem I p. 41)
field_method: Triangulation, then the detail was sketched by interpolation with a prismatic compass; the ground within 8-10 miles of camp was divided between the surveyors, all mounted (Mem I pp. 29-31). Rates were 50-660 square miles a month (p. 30). Memoirs were written from the officers' field notes and abstracts of about forty works (pp. 37-38).
search_unit: The one-inch map sheet; one entry per named place, located by a lettered square (Mem I p. 41); squares are about 7 x 9 km (kohlit/README.md, Stage 1b)
position_recording: Square letters only; relations within a place are given in words
feature_recording: Free-text entries in alphabetical order, with plans of some buildings
absence_statement_form: Free-text sentences, e.g. 'no tombs were found' (Mem II p. 236)
what_absences_cover: The named place and what the officers saw around it. No search radius is stated.
notes: Packet page numbers for SWP come from OCR running heads. The S676 sentence is on printed p. 236 (Sheet XII), not p. 30.

publication_and_access: The first publication listed in WBADB for each excavated unit; 25 read, open access or supplied by the project owner (stage2/source4_access.csv, addendum_s4)
methods_pages: Each report's own; WBADB sourcebook p. 19 on what excavation reports can show
feature_classes_sought: Protocol rule 4 limits reading to the plan and the water and burial passages, with a one-hour cap
field_method: Excavation of chosen areas; reports range from a small probe to multi-season work (sourcebook p. 19)
search_unit: The excavated area (trench, area or cave)
position_recording: Plans on local grids or none; no plan could be tied to a unit point (addendum_s4, Limits)
what_absences_cover: At most the excavated area and depth. How far an excavation reflects a whole site 'cannot be simply assumed' (sourcebook p. 19).

publication_and_access: Nigro, Sala and Taha (eds) 2011, Archaeological Heritage in the Jericho Oasis (ROSAPAT 07), public download (hash in kohlit/README.md)
methods_pages: pp. v-vi (method, database, site records), p. 3 (field activities), p. 95 (catalogue)
periods_sought: All periods, on the oasis periodization (p. v; Tab. 1.1, p. 4)
feature_classes_sought: Sites and monuments, plus scattered tombs, caves and ruins (p. 95); per period: site type, public, domestic and funerary architecture (p. vi)
field_method: A compilation of archaeological, epigraphic and literary sources, checked in the field over about ten years (p. v); surveys east of Tell es-Sultan in 1997 and 2009 (p. 3)
search_unit: The catalogue entry (a site or a monument)
